reason: The hypothesis relies on three key premises. E1 supports the first premise by showing that the as-cast lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA achieves high strength and ductility. E2 directly supports the second and third premises by demonstrating that tailored thermo-mechanical processing of the same alloy creates an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with retained lamellar character, and attributes the enhanced properties to the stated mechanisms. All premises are accurately represented by the cited evidence.
premises: Eutectic high-entropy alloys can be designed with a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure that gives high strength and ductility at room temperature.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that retains the lamellar composite nature.
The improved mechanical response in the processed alloy is due to a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
